Level 2 — Inputs are other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly (i.e. as prices) or indirectly (i.e. derived from prices).

Level 2 — Inputs are other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly (i.e. as prices) or indirectly (i.e. derived from prices).
Level 3 — Inputs are not based on observable market data (unobservable inputs). Fair values are determined in whole or in part using a valuation model based on assumptions that are neither supported by prices from observable current market transactions in the same instrument nor are they based on available market data. A) Consolidation of PSPL ESOP Management Trust (THE ‘TRUST’)

A) Consolidation of PSPL ESOP Management Trust (THE ‘TRUST’)
The Company had formulated an Employee Stock option Plan (ESOP) where the company granted an stock options to employees and the shares will be issued to employees at the time of exercising the options through PSPL ESOP Management Trust (the ‘Trust’). The Company has granted a loan to the Trust for acquisition of shares of the Company and those shares will be issued to employees at the time of exercising options under Stock Option Plan. The Trust was identified as a subsidiary. Accordingly, in the standalone financial statements, the Company had adopted the policy of considering the trust as a legal entity separate from the Company and therefore, was not consolidating the Trust in the standalone financial statements. The Company recognised the loan given to the Trust as financial asset and tested it for impairment on a periodic basis in accordance with the requirements of applicable accounting standards. However, given that the Trust was identified as a subsidiary, in the consolidated financial statements of the Company, the Trust was consolidated and consequently, the related loan to Trust (including interest) appearing in the standalone financial statements of the Company was eliminated.

During the period ended 31 December 2025, the Company changed its accounting policy whereby it decided to consolidate the Trust in the standalone financial statements to reflect a more appropriate presentation of the activity of the Trust in the standalone financial statements as the Trust carried out activities on behalf of the Company. Consequently, in the standalone financial statements of the Company, the loan given to the Trust (including interest) is eliminated.
This change in accounting policy in the standalone financial statements has been given effect by restating the comparative information for the preceding period in accordance with the requirements of applicable standards for change in accounting policy.

A very good day, everyone. We sincerely appreciate your presence and participation in today's call. Let me quickly outline the agenda for today's call.
• Sandeep will begin with an overview of our Q2 results, commentary on the business and update on our acquisition of Nagarro. • Vinit will take you through the financial details and key operational metrics for Q2. • Nitish will provide details on expansion of our AI capabilities and representative AI wins in the quarter gone by. • I will then provide an overview of our key deal wins and awards and recognitions for this quarter. • Sandeep will then come back for a quick summary of the prepared remarks, post which we will open the conference for questions.

Let me also remind you that as part of our prepared remarks and during Q&A, we may make certain statements which are forward-looking and may involve significant uncertainty. Persistent does not take any responsibility to update such forward-looking statements, and your discretion is warranted while making any investment decisions. With this, let me hand over to Sandeep for his prepared remarks.
Sandeep Kalra: Thank you, Saurabh. Good morning, good afternoon, good evening to all of you, depending on where you're joining from. I hope all of you are doing well. Let me start with a quick financial summary of the quarter gone by.
We achieved a healthy revenue growth of 7.8% quarter-on-quarter and 20% year-on-year delivering USD 487.6 million in Q2 FY27. This marks our 26th sequential quarter of revenue growth. In rupee terms, the growth for the quarter came in at 8.4% quarter-on-quarter and 30.3% year-on-year. In constant currency terms, the growth for the quarter was 7.8% quarter-on- quarter and 20.8% year-on-year. The EBIT margin for the quarter came in at 15%, translating to an EBIT growth of 1.6% quarter-on-quarter and 19.5% year-on-year.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Persistent Systems Limited
chunks.text:
The operating profit after tax for the quarter came in at 10.6%, translating to a PAT growth of 2.5% quarter-on-quarter and 5% year-on-year. The reported profit after tax for the quarter came in at 7.5%. I would like to point out that the reported PAT includes exceptional one-time expenses as part of Nagarro acquisition, resulting in approximately 3.1% impact for the quarter. Vinit, our CFO, will provide a detailed colour on the financials and margin movement later in this call.
Coming to the order book for the quarter, the total contract value for the quarter stood at USD 633.5 million, with total contract value of new bookings coming in at USD 367.1 million. The annual contract value of bookings for this quarter was USD 481 million, out of which the annual contract value from new bookings contributed to USD 262.3 million. To remind everyone, both TCV and ACV numbers include all bookings, small and large, renewals as well as new bookings across existing and newer customers.
Also, as highlighted in our earlier calls, our revenue conversion on a quarterly basis is a function of ACV bookings closed in previous quarters, as well as the conversion from multi-year deals booked in previous years, which are included in our total contract value or TCV bookings that we announce on a quarterly basis.

Persistent Systems Limited
Now, let me give you some colour on our client movement across various reported categories. This quarter, we witnessed healthy year-on-year growth among our various client buckets. Our top 5 customers' revenue grew by 38.9%, top 10 by 29.9%, top 20 by 25%, top 50 by 24% and top 100 by 21.6%.
Coming to the year-on-year movement of customers across various reported buckets: Customers with annual revenues greater than 75 million remained stable at 4. Those with USD 50 million plus annual revenue remained stable at 4. Customers in the USD 20 million plus category increased from 12 to 13. Those in USD 10 million plus category increased from 25 to 34. Customers in USD 5 million plus category increased from 56 to 60 and the customers in USD 1 million plus category increased from 191 to 280. This healthy movement of customers across various revenue brackets demonstrates our team's consistent ability in cultivating deeper, more resilient partnerships with customers over time.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Persistent Systems Limited
chunks.text:
Now, coming to the details of our performance across various geographies. In terms of year-on-year growth this quarter in USD terms, North America revenue grew by 22.5%. Revenue in Europe declined 8.5% largely because of two client-specific events. One of our key clients in the European region was acquired by a larger strategic last year, which led to the ramp-down of our program with them over the last several quarters. Another engagement completed its planned ramp-down as a part of a fixed-price engagement. Both are one-off, client-specific events rather than a sign of broader geographic demand trends. Revenue in India grew by 19.4% and the rest of the world grew by 67% although on a smaller base.
Coming to industry segments growth on a year-on-year basis. This quarter's growth was led by Software, High-Tech and Emerging verticals coming in at 28.5% followed by Banking, Financial Services and Insurance at 16.2% and Healthcare and Lifesciences vertical at 12% respectively on a year-on-year basis. Growth in our Software, High-Tech and Emerging Industries vertical was driven by our new software reinvention offering launched during the quarter underpinned by the theme of the large deal that we announced last quarter.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Persistent Systems Limited

As you know, high-tech is an industry that is most affected by advances in AI. Enterprise software companies as well as enterprises are rethinking how software is built and maintained. Our Software Reinvention offering is designed to help software and technology companies deliver AI native

products as well as modernize their legacy products for an AI first world. This is traditionally a segment where Persistent has always been significantly ahead of our peers, and we are confident that this offering will drive growth across the business creating a significant mode for us over the next several years. My colleague Nitish will cover it in more detail on this offering in the AI updates section a little later in this call.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Persistent Systems Limited
chunks.text: Let me now provide you with an update on the agreement to acquire Nagarro that we announced earlier in June this year. As you may be aware, we signed a business combination agreement in late June time frame with Nagarro, a leading European digital engineering firm aimed at creating an AI-led global engineering powerhouse serving clients with end-to-end capabilities with over $2.9 billion in revenue run rate and 46,000 plus professionals across 40 countries. To refresh everyone on the acquisition rationale, the combination provides us with expanded capabilities across multiple industry verticals and service lines, more balanced geographic mix across North America, Europe and rest of the world, strengthened near- shore European delivery footprint with presence across Romania, Portugal, Hungary and Poland, and positions us nicely as a truly global partner for large transformation programs with our global 2000 customers and prospects. This is further backed by strong cultural alignment between the two organizations anchored in entrepreneurial ethos and engineering-first culture and decades of trust with marquee clients. We are confident that this combination positions Persistent and Nagarro for the next chapter of sustained profitable growth together.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Persistent Systems Limited
chunks.text:
Let me now provide you with the progress made since the last quarter in terms of the process as some of you may be tracking the closure timelines closely. Starting with the open offer update. The initial acceptance period for voluntary public takeover offer for Nagarro began on August 6th, 2026 and ended on September 17th. The additional acceptance period began on September 23rd and ended on October 6th. We have secured approximately 94.04% of Nagarro share capital excluding treasury shares at the expiry of the additional acceptance period, significantly exceeding the minimum acceptance threshold of 50% + 1 share that we had set. Having secured more than 90% of Nagarro share capital and voting rights, we intend doing a squeeze out of the remaining minority shareholders of Nagarro upon closing.
From a merger control clearance perspective, we have received all merger control clearances and all FDI clearances other than Austria and Spain. We are confident of getting these approvals in over the next several weeks. We
Page 5 of 25

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Persistent Systems Limited
chunks.text:
Persistent Systems Limited
have also submitted the application for Reserve Bank of India's approval and we are following the due process to get the approval thereof.
In terms of financing, we intend replacing the Euro 1.4 billion 18-month bridge loan with longer tenure, capital and favorable terms. As a part of this long-term financing strategy, we will be raising USD 1.25 billion in terms of both debt and equity. Out of this, USD 450 million will be raised through equity, qualified institutional placement or equity-linked instruments like FCCB or combination of similar instruments. We have received the shareholder approval for the above funding mix at the Extraordinary General Meeting held on October 5th. We sincerely believe that the combined persistent Nagarro group presents a significant value creation opportunity for all our shareholders, clients, partners and employees.
As a part of this acquisition, I would like to highlight an important aspect around one-time expenses related to the transaction. Overall, we are expecting one-time expenses to the tune of approximately $50 million spread over three to four quarters. These expenses will weigh in on the reported EPS growth as you would have seen in our Q2 results reflecting an impact of around 3.1% on our reported PAT. We will be accounting for these expenses as they occur and will inform you all as we incur these expenses.

chunks.section: Oct 2026 earnings call · Q2 FY2027 · Persistent Systems Limited
chunks.text:
Also, as you may be aware, our ESOP vesting criteria for our team members is conditional on achieving a 12% revenue growth and a 12% EPS growth. In line with this, the Board may seek shareholders' approval to treat these one-time transaction related expenses as an exception when assessing the ESOP vesting conditions.

Software companies are facing challenges on two fronts. On one hand, they are facing challenges on growth as AI native companies and model providers compete for their customers.
